headline: High: transformers’ filesystem and shell capabilities create dangerous default interaction paths with opik’s broad network/API egress, while prompt-injection and compliance risks remain moderate due to shared data flow uncertainty.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A has no shared channel documented, but B can read/write files and run browsers, while A can call REST APIs and has broad egress. If B ingests A-produced files or API outputs as trusted instructions, prompt injection becomes plausible. The pairwise bridge is inferred, not directly evidenced, so uncertainty pushes above low.
conditions: IF B consumes files or browser content produced by A as instructions
IF A’s REST API outputs are copied into B’s prompt or pipeline without provenance checks
mitigations: Add provenance tags to A outputs before B reads them
Restrict B to allowlisted input directories
Strip instruction-like text from A outputs before handoff
Use a manual review step for any A-to-B content transfer
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and provenance enforcement in the orchestrator

B_data_leakage.rationale: A has broad network egress and B can read the filesystem and process multimodal files. No sensitive data class is listed for A, but B touches text, audio, images, video, and can exfiltrate whatever it reads if fed shared files. The leakage path exists in default-capable tooling, though the exact shared workspace is not documented.
conditions: IF A and B share a workspace or file handoff
IF B is given files containing sensitive text, audio, images, or video
mitigations: Separate A and B workspaces
Disable automatic file pickup by B
Review any shared artifacts before processing
Limit B to non-sensitive sample inputs
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: B has unrestricted filesystem write, shell, subprocess, and package-install capabilities; A has broad network egress and REST API access. Even without a documented shared directory, the pair can conflict over mutable artifacts or external resources, and B’s concurrency support increases collision risk. Because the shared mutable surface is uncertain, severity is escalated rather than lowered.
conditions: IF both agents target the same filesystem path
IF both agents modify the same external API-backed resource or repo without locking
mitigations: Assign disjoint directories to each agent
Serialize writes through one coordinator
Disable concurrent B instances on shared jobs
Use file locks for mutable artifacts
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination for shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: B can act on files and scripts, while A can emit API-driven outputs that may be treated as upstream evidence. If B consumes A’s outputs without verification, errors can cascade into downstream processing. The pairwise dependency is inferred from their I/O surfaces rather than directly documented, so medium is the conservative choice.
conditions: IF B uses A-generated outputs as authoritative inputs
IF downstream scripts or model runs are triggered from B’s processed artifacts
mitigations: Require validation of A outputs before B uses them
Add checksum or schema checks on handoff files
Keep A outputs read-only until reviewed
Log source provenance for every B input
requires-engineering: implement verification gates in the pipeline

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and list no secrets, OAuth scopes, or regulated data classes, so there is no direct residency or certification mismatch evidenced. However, B’s broad egress and file access could create compliance issues if sensitive data is introduced later. A is not cited separately because it has no listed regulated-data surface to compare.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into B’s filesystem inputs
IF deployment policy requires residency or retention controls not present in the host environment
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in shared inputs
Document retention settings for B outputs
Restrict network egress where possible
Review deployment region and storage policy
requires-engineering: add compliance controls for regulated datasets
